additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly calls this the bechina of the dynamic: 'וְזֶה בְּחִינַת: וּפַרְעֹה הִקְרִיב — שֶׁהִקְרִיב אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לַאֲבִיהֶם שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם'. Pharaoh's act of pursuit (which is the act of bringing near) is the paradigm case and bechina-name for the entire dynamic. The verse from Exodus 14:10 functions as the Torah's canonical label for the pursuit-becomes-closeness dynamic. Belongs to Package 1.

additions.reason: The Rebbe states the principle and immediately calls the Psalm verse its bechina: 'הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּכָל מָקוֹם, בִּבְחִינַת (תהילים קל״ט:ח׳)'. This is the theological foundation that enables the entire dynamic: Hashem being in every place means every act of fleeing is a fleeing toward Hashem. Dominant node of Package 2.

analysis_notes.structural_note: Torah LM2/13 is among the shortest Torahs in Likutay Moharan — a two-paragraph teaching built on one paradox: persecution = closeness. The Rebbe provides two explicit bechina anchors: (1) Hashem's omnipresence = Psalm 139:8; (2) the entire persecution-flight-closeness dynamic = ופרעה הקריב (Exodus 14:10, as interpreted in Midrash Rabbah Beshalach para. 21). The Torah functions as a single concentrated insight rather than a multi-stage argument.
